## 7



## What goes in git

The `.gitignore` for a project of this shape:

```{.default filename=".gitignore"}
.snakemake/
rds/
out/
logs/
benchmarks/
build/
```

Same rule as @sec-shape --- git is for source, not output --- which puts the
compiled PDF on the ignored side of the line along with everything else. It is
produced by running `latexmk`, so it is output, however much it feels like the
point of the project. Commit the code, the `.tex` files, and `config.yaml`; the
claim that the rest is regenerable is now enforced by a program rather than by
your recollection.

The awkward case is a simulation that takes three days, which colleagues who clone
the repository cannot rebuild over coffee. The answer is still not to commit it.
Send them `rds/`, or keep it somewhere outside the repository that the Snakefile
knows how to find; either way it travels beside the repository rather than inside
it. This is the payoff for keeping `rds/` separate from `out/` --- you hand over
the expensive half on its own, and every figure, table and PDF rebuilds from it in
seconds. @sec-scaling covers the mechanics.

## Making LaTeX quiet

Two flags in that rule are there for the sake of your terminal:

`-interaction=nonstopmode` stops LaTeX from halting at an error to ask you what to
do. In a pipeline, an interactive prompt is a hang, not a question.

`> {log} 2>&1` sends the several hundred lines LaTeX produces to `logs/paper-latexmk.log`.
When the build fails, the error is in there, and `latexmk` also leaves the more
readable `build/paper.log`.

## Raw data is read-only

The first rule reads `data/trial.csv` and never writes to it. That is not a
Snakemake requirement; it is the convention that makes everything else work, and it
deserves stating plainly: **the raw file stays exactly as it arrived.** Every
correction, exclusion and recoding happens in code, downstream, where it can be read
and argued with.

Note also what is *not* in the Snakefile. `data/make-raw-data.R`, which generated
the CSV for this example, is not a rule. If it were, Snakemake would treat the raw
data as something it could regenerate, and would do so --- silently discarding the
real file the moment it decided it was out of date. Anything you cannot afford to
lose should be an input to your pipeline and never an output of it.
